headline: **Do not read these as protection effects yet.** The placebos (gate 6) show that the model attributes a regional trend shared by protected and reference stations to protection. Reference stations relabelled as protected give placebo "effects" of -0.54 (red urchin), +0.77 (lobster) and +0.43 (sheephead) under `rw`, in the same direction as the rows above; purple urchin gives +0.06. So: purple urchin is the only taxon whose estimate is not shadowed by a placebo of the same sign; about half of the red urchin estimate and about 40% of the lobster estimate could be regional trend; the sheephead estimate is no larger than its placebo. Two further caveats. Urchins: the count layer fails the predictive checks (gate 8). Large effects: simulations with a true effect the size of the lobster estimate recover it 0.26 too low with 81% coverage (gate 5). The two priors disagree for urchins: under `rw` both urchin intervals exclude zero, under `piecewise` neither does. In simulation with a true E10 of -0.65, `rw` recovers -0.54 on average with 92% coverage; `piecewise` recovers -0.26 with 65% coverage. `piecewise` is a lower bound on size, not an alternative estimate.
gate3: **Cause.** The count model is a negative binomial with dispersion written as `inv_sqrt_phi`; as that parameter goes to zero the counts become Poisson and the likelihood is flat in it. During early warm-up a chain can coast a long way along that flat direction (it happened for the LTER dispersion parameter in every frozen chain; LTER has the fewest sheephead units, so the likelihood holds that parameter least tightly). Once there, phi = 1/inv_sqrt_phi^2 is astronomically large and the two lgamma sums in the likelihood cancel catastrophically. The log density becomes rounding noise, every proposal is rejected, the step size adapts to zero and the chain stays frozen wherever it was, with a log posterior 300 to 8,000 units below the working chains. It is a trapped chain, not a second mode. My first hypothesis (starting values too dispersed) was wrong: narrowing the start did not help, and a smaller initial step size only reduced the rate. **Fix.** The likelihood now uses a numerically stable form (`log1p`) and caps phi at 1e8, where the negative binomial equals the Poisson to about 1e-8. The prior on `inv_sqrt_phi` is unchanged and the likelihood is unchanged to 4e-4 log units at the cap (checked against scipy). The R-hat of 77 in the first report was this failure.
gate4: **What it took.** Attempt a (four sampler variants, 1,000 + 1,000 draws): no urchin or sheephead fit passed; station baselines (`sigma_b`) and the AR(1) persistence (`rho`) mixed worst for urchins (ESS 9 to 185) because a station's baseline and the mean of its persistent AR(1) deviations are nearly interchangeable. Attempt b: station baselines integrated out analytically for urchins (`--marg-b`; the marginal density matches brute-force integration to 1e-11), 2,000 + 2,000 draws, small initial step size, target acceptance 0.98. Lobster passed; urchins improved to ESS 200 to 380 with a few divergences. Attempt c (final code): 3,000 warm-up + 6,000 draws per chain, target acceptance 0.99. Across all 60 fits without a frozen chain, the E10 mean for a given taxon and prior varied by at most 0.05, including the fits that failed the gate. All eight reported fits come from attempt c.
gate5: **Reading.** `rw`: at no effect, a small effect and a moderate effect, the 90% intervals cover 91 to 92% of the time and the false-positive rate is 9 to 10%. For large true effects (urchin layout +2.0, lobster layout +1.93) the estimate is pulled toward zero (bias -0.46 and -0.26) and coverage falls to 0.74 and 0.81: the prior on the first four-year increment, Normal(0, 0.6), treats a jump of 1.0 to 1.2 as unlikely. `piecewise`: almost never a false positive (0 to 1%), but it under-covers moderate and large effects (0.65 at -0.65, 0.62 at +2.0, 0.77 at +1.93) because it shrinks every increment toward zero. All coverage failures are in the conservative direction: real effects are underestimated, none is invented, and no interval excluded zero with the wrong sign except 3% of `rw` replicates at the small effect. Power is low for moderate effects: a true 48% decline per decade is detected 33% of the time under `rw` and 3% under `piecewise`. Limits of this test. The simulator is the fitted model, so it shares the model's blind spots: it has no regional trend (the follow-up under gate 6 adds one and the model fails) and it uses the model's own count distribution (so it cannot show the misfit found in gate 8). The urchin-layout replicates were fitted with the first sampler settings; some variance parameter has R-hat above 1.1 in most replicates, while E10 has R-hat below 1.05 in every replicate. About three-quarters of the replicates ran before the likelihood was made numerically stable; the two versions agree to 4e-4 log units away from the Poisson limit. Widening the increment prior is a model change and was not made.
gate6_time: **Sheephead.** The off-centre placebo is in the data, not the sampler: it persists under both priors, every fake year from 1990 to 1995, with and without the level shift, and with each of the three MPAs left out in turn. In the KFM record before 2003 (three MPAs, one future-reserve station each, 7 stations in all), sheephead density at the future-reserve stations fell from 0.90 to 0.26 fish per 100 m2 between 1985-96 and 1997-2002 (-71%), while reference stations fell from 1.22 to 0.78 (-36%). The Scorpion future-reserve station recorded no sheephead in 1997-2002. The KFM fish count layout also changed in 1996 (two 200 m2 units per visit to four 100 m2 units). So protected and reference sheephead trajectories were not parallel before designation. Under `rw` the model extends that pre-existing divergence as a straight line and the interval excludes zero; under `piecewise` it shrinks and the interval includes zero. With fake year 1993 the data stop at age 9, so E10 is partly extrapolated. Consequence for the real fit: KFM protected stations enter 2003 at a low point, and any rebound would be read as a protection effect.
gate6_space: **Six of eight cells are off-centre, in the direction of the headline.** Whichever reference stations are relabelled, red urchin comes out negative, lobster positive and sheephead positive. The placebo values track the average trend at reference stations since 2003 (within-station slope of log density, stations with at least 8 survey years): red urchin -0.45 per decade (placebo -0.54), lobster +0.44 (+0.77), sheephead +0.48 (+0.43), purple urchin +0.35 with only 38% of stations positive, so no consistent trend (+0.06). The model is reading a trend that reference stations share as if it were protection.
gate7: **Finding.** Yes, for urchins. The PISCO metadata (`MLPA_kelpforest_release9.eml.xml`, swath method) states that for select species such as sea urchins, high densities are spatially subsampled and extrapolated to three 20 m2 segments of the transect, and transect notes in the raw swath files record subsampling when more than 30 urchins were counted in a segment. The delivered files hold only the extrapolated integer count per transect: there is no field for metres searched, in either the 2024 MLPA file or the 1.11 release. The area actually searched therefore cannot be recovered, and the refit asked for in the gate cannot be done as specified. **Bounding check instead.** PISCO units with a count above a cap are treated as if only cap/count of the transect had been searched (count set to the cap, area scaled down by the same factor, density unchanged). Cap 90 = 30 per segment times three segments; cap 30 is a harsher bound. Lobster and sheephead are not subsampled.
gate8: **Urchins fail.** For purple and red urchins, in KFM and PISCO, the fitted count model predicts too few zero counts (purple, KFM: 23% observed, 15% replicated; PISCO: 15% against 11%) and too heavy an upper tail (purple, PISCO 99th percentile: about 3,500 observed, 6,400 replicated). One dispersion parameter per program is stretched to cover both the empty units and the dense ones and fits neither. Likely contributors: real patchiness (many empty quadrats beside dense patches), a physical ceiling on density, and the PISCO subsampling in gate 7, which trims the upper tail. Lobster and sheephead reproduce the zero share and spread; only the PISCO 99th percentile is slightly over-predicted (lobster 10 observed against 14; sheephead 12 against 14), and the sheephead PISCO zero share is slightly under-predicted (0.457 against 0.445). The mean structure is carried by cell totals, so E10 may be less sensitive to this than the intervals are, but that is not tested. Fixing it means changing the count distribution (for example a zero-inflated or two-part count model, or a dispersion that varies with density), which is a structural decision.
gate9: **Reading.** No sensitivity changes the sign of E10 or whether its 90% interval excludes zero. The largest shift is for purple urchin under `piecewise` when Harris Point SMR is left out (-0.25 to -0.51); leaving Harris Point out moves all four taxa away from zero by 0.06 to 0.26. Webster's Arch and Wyckoff Ledge change E10 by at most 0.11. These sensitivities share the trend-leak flaw found in gate 6, so they show that E10 is stable to these choices, not that it is right.
unverified:
- **The trend leak has no remedy tested.** Until the model gives reference stations a matching common-drift term and the space placebo centres on zero, none of the E10 values can be called a protection effect. Subtracting the placebo from the headline is a rough reading, not an estimate.
- The urchin count-layer misfit (gate 8) has no remedy tested; whether it moves E10 or only its interval is unknown.
- The area actually searched in subsampled PISCO urchin transects is not in the delivered files; gate 7 is a bound, not a correction.
- Gate 9 fits use 2,000 + 2,000 draws; most do not meet the gate-4 thresholds (marked). E10 is stable across them, but their intervals are less exact than the headline fits.
- Simulation replicates use short chains (2 x 500); E10 converged in every replicate, variance parameters often did not.
- The space placebo's relabellings share most of their data, so the count of intervals excluding zero has no clean reference distribution. The verdict rule for it was written after seeing the results; it is stricter than the rule first coded.
- The trend-leak simulation used one trend size (0.8 per decade) and 40 replicates per cell.
- The predictive checks hold latent station-year densities at their posterior draws, so they test the count layer only.
- The 1996 change in the KFM fish count layout is inferred from unit areas in the data, not checked against protocol documents.
- The seven regions in `data.py` are still a proposal. No region definition, station or year was changed, and no site was dropped from any reported fit.
- No stage 2 (multi-taxon), biomass or kelp work was started.
gate6_trend: **Confirmed: this is a flaw in the model structure, not in the data.** With no protection effect and a shared trend of 0.8 per decade, `rw` reports an E10 of 0.47 to 0.69 in the direction of the trend and its 90% interval excludes zero in 23 to 60% of replicates (10% is nominal); `piecewise` reports 0.20 to 0.41 and keeps nominal coverage only because its intervals are wide relative to the leak. Why: the response curve g(age) is a drift term that all protected stations share after designation, and reference stations have no matching term. Region-year effects are independent from year to year and shrunk toward zero, and each station's AR(1) deviations are persistent enough to absorb a slow trend station by station. A common trend therefore lands in the AR(1) deviations at reference stations and in g(age) at protected stations. The gate-5 simulations missed this because the simulator had no trend. Remedy to consider (not built: it is a change to model structure): give every station the same capacity for common drift, for example a random-walk year effect shared by all stations with regional deviations, so that a trend present at reference stations is attributed to time. Then rerun the space placebo and this simulation; both should centre on zero before any E10 is shown as a protection effect.
